newsitem.title: USA: US 'gravely concerned' about northern Iraq crisis.
newsitem.headline: US 'gravely concerned' about northern Iraq crisis.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it was "gravely concerned" about instability in northern Iraq and called upon a Kurdish militia allied to Baghdad and all other groups in the region to stop fighting.
Washington also urged the governments of Iraq and Iran to "desist from activity that would aggravate the current violence and instability," State Department spokesman Nick Burns said in a statement.

Burns' statement came in response to reports that the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) of veteran warlord Massoud Barzani had taken Iraqi Kurdistan's biggest city Sulaimaniya, hastily abandoned by the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
"The United States is gravely concerned about the instability in northern Iraq, the continuing grave security situation, and the humanitarian crisis that could ensue," Burns said.
"We call upon the KDP and all other groups in northern Iraq to cease fighting and to respet the rights of all civilian populations in the area," he added.

Barzani's group, aided by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein in its capture of the PUK-held city of Arbil last month, said it now held the whole of northern Iraq, raising fears of a repeat of a mass refugee exodus into Iran and Turkey.
